title: Arrays
objective: See why reading by index is instant but inserting in the middle is slow.

sources.title: Cormen, Leiserson, Rivest and Stein, Introduction to Algorithms, 4th ed. (MIT Press, 2022): elementary data structures: arrays

simplifies: Real arrays (like Python lists) also grow by copying everything into a bigger block now and then. That cost is left out; the shifting shown here is the main idea.

quiz.prompt: Reading nums[500] in an array of 1,000 items takes…

options.explanation: Right. The position is worked out directly from the index, so any item is equally quick to read.
That is walking a linked list. An array jumps straight to the index.
No search is needed: the index says exactly where the item is.

quiz.prompt: Inserting at the front of an array of n items moves how many items?

options.explanation: Only the new item arrives, but every existing item must shift right to make room.
Right. Every item moves one place, so inserting at the front is O(n).
There is no gap at the front; items must move to make one.
